title: Letter of demand (family provision)
description: Puts the executors on notice of our client's family provision claim.
guidance:
Write to the executors of the estate, or their solicitors. We act for a person who claims that the deceased's will doesn't make adequate provision for them.

- Say who we act for and their relationship to the deceased, as the matter facts or instructions say.
- Say that our client intends to apply to the court for further provision from the estate (a family provision claim), unless the matter can be resolved.
- Ask the executors not to distribute the estate while the claim is outstanding, and to confirm that they won't.
- Ask for a copy of the will and the grant, and a statement of the estate's assets and liabilities.
- Don't state the amount or share our client seeks, any deadline for the claim, or any legal reference, unless the instructions or the matter's documents give them; use a placeholder where the letter needs one.
- Keep the tone firm and courteous. Don't predict the outcome of the claim.
